report.summary: Many gates define exit criteria that are not falsifiable as written; for example, 'no new feature path outside canonical contracts' cannot be disproven without a complete enumeration of all possible paths.
risks: 10.1 | critical | 'Work advances in order. A later-gate experiment may be prototyped only when it does not create a competing kernel and is explicitly labelled experimental.' The phrase 'competing kernel' is undefined and unfalsifiable; no observation can determine whether a prototype creates one. | Replace 'competing kernel' with a specific, testable condition (e.g., 'does not create a new event store or state store outside canonical contracts').

10.2 | high | 'Deliver: one Event Store plus content-addressed artifact store' — unfalsifiable because 'one Event Store' could be any system claiming to be an event store; no observable criteria distinguish it from a non-compliant store. | Define minimal functional tests that the store must pass (e.g., can store and retrieve events by content address).

10.3 | high | 'canonical Mission, Attempt, Evidence, Campaign, policy, and receipt schemas' — unfalsifiable because 'canonical' is subjective; there is no test to determine whether a schema is canonical. | Specify a formal validation mechanism (e.g., schema must pass a provided JSON Schema validator).

10.4 | high | 'one vendor-neutral Agent Contract / Runtime Manifest for capabilities, mission envelopes, tools, egress, workspace, cost, and conformance receipts' — unfalsifiable because 'vendor-neutral' is not defined; any claim of neutrality can be contested. | Define a set of vendors that must be able to implement the contract without modification, and test each.

10.5 | high | 'centralized start/guard path for every effectful runtime entrypoint' — unfalsifiable because 'every effectful runtime entrypoint' is not enumerated; one could always claim an unlisted entrypoint exists. | Require an explicit list of all entrypoints and a test that each passes through the guard.

10.6 | high | 'enforceable write/egress/spend/secrets/concurrency/kill policies' — unfalsifiable because 'enforceable' is not defined; no test can prove enforcement without a threat model. | Define a set of attack scenarios and show that each is prevented.

10.7 | high | 'real adapter fixtures for start, stream, tool events, structured output, timeout, cancellation, workspace isolation, and cost' — unfalsifiable because 'real' is ambiguous; any fixture could be claimed real. | Define what makes a fixture 'real' (e.g., it must execute against a live environment, not a mock).

10.8 | high | 'policy coverage tests for Claude, Codex, Ollama, Web/API, MCP/File Bridge, Python entrypoints, and isolated worktrees' — unfalsifiable because 'coverage' is not quantified; 100% coverage is not specified. | Define required coverage metric (e.g., each policy must be tested with at least one positive and one negative case per entrypoint).

10.9 | high | 'no new feature path or state store outside the canonical contracts' — unfalsifiable because 'feature path' and 'state store' are not exhaustively defined; any new path could be claimed to be within contracts by reinterpretation. | Require a formal architecture document that lists all allowed paths and stores, and a process for adding new ones only through amendments.

10.10 | high | 'Exit only when a fault-injection matrix demonstrates fail-closed protected effects and fail-open read-only inspection.' — unfalsifiable because 'fault-injection matrix' is not specified; any matrix could be claimed sufficient. | Define the exact set of faults to inject and the expected behavior for each (e.g., 'inject network partition; assert that writes fail with timeout, reads succeed with stale data').

10.11 | medium | 'Prove one vertical mission: propagate Event.voltage -> bias_voltage across Python, Markdown, and CSV. Ikarus produces one MissionContract; the four planes produce two typed WorkItems; attempts run in isolation; restart/replay works; tests, schema checks, and link checks produce an EvidencePacket. No auto-merge.' — Most sub-claims are falsifiable but 'restart/replay works' is vague; 'works' is not defined. | Define specific success criteria for restart/replay (e.g., after restart, replay produces identical state to original run).

10.12 | medium | 'Add function/method resolution, data/schema extraction, knowledge crosslinks, revision atomicity, evidence locators, and four-plane ablations.' — Unfalsifiable because 'add' does not specify what it means to have these features; no test to verify they are correctly implemented. | For each feature, define a minimal test (e.g., 'function/method resolution: given a function call, the system returns the correct implementation').

10.13 | medium | 'Do not scale before the full graph beats simpler representations.' — Unfalsifiable because 'beats' is not defined; no comparison metric or threshold is given. | Define a specific benchmark and success metric (e.g., 'on task X, full graph achieves higher success rate than bag-of-words baseline with p<0.05').

10.14 | medium | 'Freeze public tasks, evaluator versions, budgets, model/hardware reporting, seed policy, and statistical reporting.' — Unfalsifiable because 'freeze' does not specify what it means to be frozen; changes could be made that are claimed as not breaking freeze. | Define a mechanism to detect changes (e.g., checksums of frozen files) and a process to update them only through amendments.

10.15 | medium | 'Required baselines are Random Search, Best-of-N, a single-LLM loop, simple local mutation, BM25, embeddings, code-only graph, four separate indices, evaluator-only selection, archive/MAP-Elites, and a transparent AlphaEvolve-like proxy.' — Unfalsifiable because 'transparent AlphaEvolve-like proxy' is not defined; no criteria for what counts as 'like'. | Define the proxy's algorithm and parameters explicitly (e.g., 'a genetic algorithm with population size 100, mutation rate 0.1, etc.').

10.16 | medium | 'Measure success rate, best-so-far AUC, wall time, tokens, compute, variance, diversity, regressions, and human intervention.' — Unfalsifiable because 'human intervention' is not defined; any observation could be claimed as intervention. | Define what constitutes human intervention (e.g., any manual parameter change during a run) and require logging.

10.17 | medium | 'Test Graph-conditioned Representation Search first: use verified Project Twin structure to select and compress context or operators, then compare against budget-equal retrieval and evaluator-only baselines.' — Unfalsifiable because 'use' does not specify how the structure is used; any usage could be claimed. | Define the exact algorithm (e.g., 'select top-k nodes by PageRank from the Project Twin graph').
10.18 | medium | 'Freeze generator, model, token budget, and evaluator.' — Unfalsifiable because 'freeze' is not defined as above. | Same as 10.14.

10.19 | medium | 'Controls include edge rewiring, relation-label permutation, cross-plane bridges off, stale snapshots, and an oracle graph.' — Unfalsifiable because 'stale snapshots' is not defined; what makes a snapshot stale? | Define a specific delay or version lag that constitutes stale (e.g., 'snapshot taken more than 24 hours before the experiment').

10.20 | medium | 'One hypothesis, one pre-registered protocol, complete ablations.' — Unfalsifiable because 'complete ablations' is not defined; what set of ablations is complete? | Require that all controls listed in 10.19 are tested, and define 'complete' as covering all combinations of control variables.

10.21 | medium | 'Release reproducible task definitions, evaluator code/version, receipts, cost/latency tables, ablations, failures, and a claim bounded by observed evidence.' — Unfalsifiable because 'reproducible' is not defined; what makes a task definition reproducible? | Require that the release includes all code, data, and instructions needed to reproduce the results, and that a third party can verify.

10.22 | medium | 'AlphaEvolve is closed, so a broad framework comparison is not scientifically available.' — Falsifiable but unclear: 'not scientifically available' is a claim that could be tested by attempting to do the comparison and failing due to lack of access. However, as a statement of fact, it is falsifiable by gaining access. | Attempt to obtain AlphaEvolve code or results; if accessible, the claim is false.

10.23 | medium | '“Beats AlphaEvolve” is permitted only for directly comparable public artifact scores under budget-equal measurements; otherwise state the narrower proxy/task result.' — Falsifiable: one can check whether a claim of beating AlphaEvolve meets these criteria. However, 'directly comparable' is vague. | Define what makes artifact scores directly comparable (e.g., same task, same metric, same budget).
todos: Define 'competing kernel' in section 10.1 with a testable condition.
Specify exit criteria for Gate 0 as a concrete fault-injection matrix (list of faults and expected outcomes).
Define 'freeze' for gates 3 and 4 as a mechanism (e.g., version-controlled files with change detection).
Replace 'beats' in 10.13 with a specific metric and threshold.
Define 'stale snapshots' in 10.19 with a quantitative criterion.

claims.claim: Work advances in order. A later-gate experiment may be prototyped only when it does not create a competing kernel and is explicitly labelled experimental.
claims.why: The term 'competing kernel' is undefined. No observation can determine whether a prototype creates one, because there is no criterion to distinguish a competing kernel from a non-competing one. A falsifiable version would define 'competing kernel' (e.g., 'a kernel that implements a subset of the canonical contracts with different semantics').

claims.claim: Deliver: one Event Store plus content-addressed artifact store;
claims.why: The claim does not specify what it means to 'deliver' an Event Store. Any system that claims to be an event store could be considered delivered. To be falsifiable, there must be a test suite that the store must pass (e.g., can store and retrieve events, content-addressing works as specified).

claims.claim: canonical Mission, Attempt, Evidence, Campaign, policy, and receipt schemas;
claims.why: 'Canonical' is subjective; there is no test to determine whether a schema is canonical. A falsifiable version would define the schemas formally (e.g., as JSON Schema files) and require that they are used without deviation.
